comment: The revert-check of the case-name traceability rule (`tools/check-case-names.sh`, issue #896): one record per rule the check states, so each refusal is proven to fire on the line that stops it. Run it with `bash tools/mutate.sh --mutations tools/tests/check-case-names-mutations.json`; `.pi/skills/revert-check` owns the rule and `.pi/skills/mutation-runner` owns how. `case-cmd` runs one named case of the check's own self-test (`--case {case}`), so a mutation pays one case and not the suite. Every search is a single line and unique in its file, because the runner's replacement is literal and line-based, and the file is restored byte for byte afterwards. The four rules are: a name no harness lists is refused (record 1), a full name two harnesses list is refused (record 2), a row whose list is absent is refused instead of read as empty (record 3), and an unclaimed case is a number that refuses nothing (record 4).

mutations.label: unresolved-name-is-refused
mutations.search: if (!(nm in decl)) { print "unresolved\t" $2 "\t" $3 "\t" $4 "\t" $5 "\t" nm; next }
mutations.why: a `**Case**:` line naming a case no declared harness lists is the dead reference this capability exists to refuse; without the refusal the check would resolve a name that exists nowhere and report ok

mutations.label: duplicate-full-name-is-refused
mutations.why: an identical full name in two harnesses makes the resolution a coin toss, so it is refused with both names rather than resolved from whichever row was read last

mutations.label: absent-list-is-refused
mutations.search: if [ -z "$path" ] || [ ! -f "$root/$path" ]; then problem rows "$id — $path is not in the tree"; return; fi
mutations.replace: if false; then problem rows "$id — $path is not in the tree"; return; fi
mutations.why: a row whose case list has moved or been deleted would otherwise declare nothing and read as an empty harness, which turns every one of its spec references into a dead reference the check cannot see

mutations.label: an-unclaimed-case-never-refuses
mutations.search: for (c in cases) if (!(c in claimed)) print "unclaimed\t" c
mutations.replace: for (c in cases) if (!(c in claimed)) print "unresolved\t" c
mutations.why: a case that proves its harness rather than a requirement is not a defect: the count is printed and the exit status stays 0, because a check that refused 5985 unclaimed cases would be turned off in a day
